source_snapshot.procedure: Generate seconds with `date +%s`, convert the 32-bit value to four little-endian bytes, send `ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x49 <bytes>` locally, then run Get SEL Time.
source_snapshot.criteria: The command completes without error and the time is set correctly.
source_snapshot.deepseek_finding: DeepSeek appropriately marks the clock mutation as user-request-only and requires read-back, but its proposed high-level shell command neither preserves the source's raw encoding validation nor resolves the IPMI local-time/UTC-offset behavior.

original_test_intent.purpose: Validate that the BMC accepts an in-band Set SEL Time command with a correctly encoded four-byte timestamp and that Get SEL Time reads back the intended SEL timestamp clock value.
original_test_intent.target: The selected SUT BMC's SEL timestamp clock through the local in-band IPMI interface; the host clock itself is a trusted reference and is not a mutation target.
original_test_intent.scope: Preserve the current SEL clock, UTC-offset state and event chronology, set one approved current-time value using Storage net function 0x0A command 0x49 with four little-endian bytes, read the value back within a defined time window, verify offset/chronology effects, and leave the BMC clock under the approved lab time policy.
original_test_intent.operation: Determine whether the platform stores SEL time as relative local seconds or follows an OEM UTC convention, read current SEL time and supported UTC offset, generate the target value from a trusted synchronized clock under that model, record a timestamp-clock-change event pair where supported, write once, re-read the clock and offset, compare against the send/receive interval, then restore a correct current value and offset only under the approved policy.
original_test_intent.duration_and_iterations: The workbook estimates 10 attended and 5 machine minutes and describes one set followed by one get. No repeated clock shifting, boundary sweep or automatic retry is authorized.
original_test_intent.expected_result: The write completes successfully; the read-back value advances normally and falls within the approved reference interval and tolerance under the selected time model; the intended UTC offset is restored because Set SEL Time resets it to unspecified in the standard model; paired chronology evidence and subsequent SEL timestamps remain interpretable.
original_test_intent.required_evidence: Approval and maintenance window; BMC/firmware/local-interface identity; trusted host time, timezone and synchronization status; before/target/after raw and decoded SEL times; pre/post UTC offset; exact little-endian request; completion/read-back/tolerance; preserved SEL export and timestamp-clock synchronization event evidence; final clock/offset/chronology health and recovery decision.
ambiguities: The source calls `date +%s` a local-time value, but that command returns a Unix epoch independent of the display timezone while the IPMI timestamp format is defined as relative local time unless an applicable UTC-offset/platform convention is established.
The source does not read or restore the SEL Time UTC Offset, although the standard says Set SEL Time automatically resets that offset to unspecified.
`The time should be set correctly` supplies no reference-clock quality, comparison interval, tolerance or drift rule.
The source requests log clearing even though the test changes event chronology and requires preserved before/after evidence.
The source does not define the final desired clock value after the test; restoring the exact pre-test numeric value would move the clock backward by the elapsed test duration.
source_conflicts: The procedure's `date +%s` conversion is presented as local seconds without defining the BMC's local-time versus UTC/offset model, so the supplied value can conflict with the criterion that SEL time be set correctly.

v2_review_conclusion.finding: V2 correctly treats this as an approved mutation, preserves the SEL baseline, requires explicit time basis, structured little-endian encoding, read-back and chronology protection, and rejects log clearing. It misses the normative side effect that Set SEL Time resets the SEL UTC offset to unspecified, does not require timestamp-clock synchronization event pairs, and could be read as restoring the stale pre-test numeric value rather than a current policy-correct clock.

applicable_history.decision: Historical guidance requires user confirmation for SEL-time mutation. No user ruling fixes a universal UTC/local model or authorizes clearing evidence.

v3_review_conclusion.summary: Keep the V2 capability class but add the missing SEL-time model and offset lifecycle. Execution requires the platform's local-versus-UTC convention, trusted reference/tolerance, maintenance approval and qualified clock-change evidence; after the one write, the runner must verify or restore the UTC offset and finish at the current approved time, not the stale baseline value.

available_now: The source fixes the standard Set SEL Time command and four-byte little-endian request format.
IPMI 2.0 defines Set/Get SEL Time, the relative-local timestamp model, UTC-offset commands and the automatic offset reset caused by Set SEL Time.
Current SEL time, UTC offset, SEL export and host time synchronization can be collected read-only before approval.
missing_inputs: Platform/BMC policy for SEL relative-local versus OEM UTC interpretation and applicability of Get/Set SEL Time UTC Offset
Trusted reference clock, synchronization status, timezone/DST policy, exact target-generation rule, acceptable read-back latency/tolerance and final desired time/offset state
Maintenance window, confirmation that no incident hold or concurrent chronology-dependent test is active, and approval to mutate the clock
Qualified raw encoder/parser, paired timestamp-clock synchronization event method or documented platform alternative, protected access, evidence retention and recovery/escalation procedure
execution_readiness_detail.input_owner: The BMC/platform owner defines timestamp and UTC-offset semantics; the lab/time-service owner supplies the trusted reference and final policy; the security/incident owner clears evidence holds; the testcase owner approves the mutation and acceptance tolerance.
safe_read_only_work_before_closure: Read BMC identity, current SEL time, UTC offset, SDR clock relationship where applicable, time-service status and export the existing SEL without clearing it.
Validate four-byte encoding, interval-based comparison and offset-restoration logic offline with synthetic values, including DST/offset and 32-bit-range cases.
prohibited_until_closed: Do not set SEL time, clear logs, change the host clock, assume `date +%s` matches the BMC's local-time model, omit offset handling, overwrite chronology during an evidence hold, auto-retry or restore the stale captured integer.
Do not claim success from completion code alone or leave the final SEL clock/offset outside the approved lab time policy.
execution_readiness_detail.closure_verification: Owners approve the platform time model, reference, tolerance, chronology method and final-state policy; the runner proves little-endian encoding and interval comparison; pre/post offset handling is explicit; the SEL export and change-event pair/alternative are ready; rollback means restoring current correct time plus offset, not replaying the old timestamp.

revision_candidate.test_name: In-Band SEL Timestamp Clock Set, Read-Back, and Offset Validation
revision_candidate.purpose: Set one approved SEL timestamp through the local IPMI interface, verify its four-byte encoding and bounded read-back against a trusted reference, and preserve an interpretable event chronology and correct UTC-offset state.
revision_candidate.applicable_platform_environment: The exact server/BMC firmware with documented SEL local-time/UTC behavior, a working in-band IPMI interface, synchronized trusted reference clock, preserved SEL and an approved maintenance window without an evidence hold.
revision_candidate.target_scope: The BMC SEL timestamp clock and its associated UTC-offset state only. The host clock, unrelated logs, BMC timezone policy and existing SEL records must not be rewritten or cleared.
revision_candidate.required_inputs: BMC timestamp/offset model; current and final time policy; trusted reference and sync status; timezone/DST and UTC offset; target-generation rule and tolerance; exact raw encoder/parser; clock-change event procedure; baseline export; approval, retention and recovery plan.
revision_candidate.test_command_procedure_intent: Read and preserve SEL time, UTC offset and SEL chronology. After fresh approval, derive one target from the trusted reference under the documented platform model, encode it as unsigned 32-bit little-endian and record the pre-change synchronization event where supported. Send `ipmitool raw 0x0a 0x49 <LSB> <byte1> <byte2> <MSB>` once, immediately read back SEL time and UTC offset, generate/verify the post-change event, compare read-back against the reference send/receive interval, and set the approved UTC offset or current policy-correct final time only as explicitly authorized.
revision_candidate.preconditions: Correct BMC and firmware verified; in-band path and qualified tool available; reference clock synchronized; platform time/offset semantics and tolerance signed; current SEL/offset/export captured; no incident hold or competing event-correlation run; one-write approval and recovery owner active.
revision_candidate.expected_evidence: Approval; BMC/firmware/tool identity; reference synchronization and timezone model; before/target/read-back/final raw and decoded values; exact request bytes and completion; send/receive timestamps and tolerance result; before/after UTC offset; SEL export and paired clock-change events or documented alternative; final chronology and clock health.
revision_candidate.acceptance_reference: Intel IPMI 2.0 rev. 1.1 sections 31.10, 31.11, 31.11a, 31.11b and 37 plus the exact BMC firmware's timekeeping policy and owner-approved tolerance/final-state rule.
revision_candidate.safety_restrictions: Never clear SEL or host logs, alter host time, guess timezone semantics, write during an evidence hold, omit the offset reset check, repeat the mutation automatically, set invalid/special timestamp ranges, or restore the old captured integer after time has advanced.
revision_candidate.human_approval_requirements: Fresh BMC/lab owner approval is required for the exact target policy, chronology impact, UTC offset, maintenance window and final-state/recovery plan before the clock write.
revision_candidate.manual_boundaries: Owners decide the platform time model, evidence-hold status, acceptable tolerance and final clock policy. With those inputs, encoding, one write, immediate read-back, offset verification and evidence capture can be automated; chronology disputes remain an engineer decision.
revision_candidate.recovery_requirements: On mismatch or offset/chronology failure, stop without automatic retry, preserve all evidence and use the trusted reference to restore the current policy-correct SEL time and offset only with owner authorization. Do not set the host clock or erase events; escalate if event ordering cannot be reconciled.
revision_candidate.stop_conditions: Target mismatch; unclear local/UTC model; unsynchronized reference; active evidence hold; missing baseline/export or approval; invalid/special/out-of-range target; encoding mismatch; command failure; read-back outside tolerance; unexpected offset reset behavior; missing chronology events; concurrent clock change; inability to establish a safe current final state.

identified_defects: The source conflates Unix epoch output with IPMI relative-local timestamp semantics and omits the platform conversion policy.
V2 does not account for the standard-mandated reset of SEL Time UTC Offset to unspecified after Set SEL Time.
Neither source nor V2 requires the recommended before/after timestamp-clock synchronization event pair for preserving chronology.
The source defines no tolerance, trusted reference or final-state rule, and V2's restore wording could allow replay of a stale time.
The source's log-clear instruction is incompatible with audit and chronology validation.
reason_for_change: Retain the approved-mutation classification while closing a real timekeeping defect: Set SEL Time changes both the timestamp clock and, normatively, the associated offset state. A correct verifier must use the platform's time model, compare against a timed reference interval, preserve clock-change chronology and restore a current correct state rather than a stale number.

new_technical_evidence.title: Intelligent Platform Management Interface Specification v2.0 rev. 1.1 E7 Markup
new_technical_evidence.version: 2.0 rev. 1.1, Errata 7; sections 31.10-31.11b, 37, and Timestamp Clock Synchronization event note
new_technical_evidence.applicability: BMC/SEL devices implementing the standard time and optional UTC-offset commands; exact OEM time policy must still be confirmed
new_technical_evidence.supports: SEL time is a four-byte little-endian timestamp used for event logging; IPMI timestamps are relative local time, Set SEL Time resets the associated UTC offset to unspecified, and paired clock-synchronization events are recommended around a timestamp change to preserve relative chronology.
new_technical_evidence.remaining_uncertainty: This BMC's UTC-offset command support, OEM UTC/local behavior, NTP interaction, SDR-clock linkage and event-generation implementation remain platform-specific.

removed_ambiguities: Separates Unix epoch generation from the BMC's relative-local/UTC-offset storage policy.
Defines interval-based read-back acceptance instead of an unspecified `set correctly` assertion.
Defines final recovery as current policy-correct time plus offset, not the pre-test integer.
resolved_blockers: The write/read mechanics and four-byte encoding are standard and automatable once the platform time model and approval are supplied.
remaining_blockers: No clock mutation may run until the platform's time/offset semantics, trusted reference, tolerance, chronology preservation, maintenance approval and final-state recovery are explicit.
objective_improvement_over_v2: V3 preserves V2's safety gates while adding the otherwise missed UTC-offset reset, clock-change event evidence and non-stale recovery rule; these affect actual SEL timestamp correctness, not writing style.

agent_understanding_result.notes: Isolated validation confirmed the set/read/offset intent, unsigned 32-bit little-endian encoding, authoritative bounded reference time, SEL chronology preservation, policy-correct final state, one-write/no-automatic-retry boundary, evidence, stop conditions, and false-PASS protections. Remaining time-model, tolerance, and approval data are platform handoff requirements.

per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_purpose_fact: The row builds four little-endian bytes for raw Storage command 49h, then reads SEL time back.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_v2_comparison: V2 protects chronology and encoding but omits the UTC-offset reset and a safe current-time recovery rule.
per_case_integrity_check.source_specific_safety_evidence_decision: Allow only baseline/export and offline encoder work before approval; one clock write is permitted only with platform time semantics, paired chronology evidence, offset restoration and bounded read-back.
